Shape: an approved write is a command flow (flows/<name>.yaml with a `command:` block) bound to a tool with handler {kind: flow, operation: command}, effect write and approval first_party (or grant, see `connector_approval`). Every command flow needs the three jobs `prepare`, `apply` and `readback` and 1 to 64 `dependencies` (an insert-only command still names one, for example the row it must not duplicate); review refuses `missing "readback"`, `missing "dependencies"` and `dependencies must contain 1..64 entries`. A command flow has no route of its own: the app's own forms and pages cannot run it. The file name is the command's name: `flows/<name>.yaml` where <name> starts with a lowercase letter and holds only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, 1 to 64 characters (`flows/receive_stock.yaml`; a hyphen, capital letter or dot is refused). Once the app has an mcp.yaml, every command flow must be bound by exactly one tool in it: one that no tool binds, or that two bind, is refused with `command "<name>" requires exactly one declaration binding`; in an app with no mcp.yaml a command flow loads without a connector, cannot run, and still guards the columns it owns (`connector_owned_fields`). The dependency query shape is in `dependency_shape`, and the required ENCRYPTION_KEY in `command_encryption_key`.

Listing and permissions: only while the owner approved-writes switch is on, /api/_mcp lists each admitted command tool plus the framework tools _commit and _status, and only to a grant whose scopes and current role both carry the declared write permissions. A command permission is `<table>:read|write` for a declared table, or `<capability>:<action>` where some role in app.yaml `roles:` grants that capability resource, directly or through inherits, so a typo is refused; the action is any identifier and at least one permission must be a declared write table's `:write` or a capability's `:write`. Wildcard permissions are refused, and runtime checks are the same scope intersection as for tables. Holding the permission is all the runtime asks of the caller before the command's SQL runs: the table's `access:` rule and row scope are not applied to a command, so its SQL carries the owner, tenant and role predicate itself (`connector_hooks_effects`, 'Access rules are not applied'). Resource metadata, registration and consent offer those write scopes only while the switch is on, and a read grant never gains them.
Command SQL: what it may bind, call and touch (actor and parameter bindings, the SQL function list, tables, generated values, framework and app triggers) is in `connector_command_sql`.

Prepare: calling a command tool only prepares. It returns {operation_id, preview, expires_at, review_url} with a fixed 15-minute expiry and writes no business data. What happens next is in `connector_approval` and `connector_commit`.

Refuse in prepare: a command's prepare phase may refuse with the author's message. An `if` branch (or its `else`) holding exactly one `run: respond` with a literal `status` 400-499 (not 401 or 407) and `json: {error: '<literal text, 1-500 characters, no template or control characters>'}` ends the prepare before any operation, approval or write exists, and the tool fails with that message under invalid_input (400, 422), conflict (409) or denied (any other 4xx, such as 403 or 404). Any other mid-phase respond (a for_each loop body, nested ifs included, may hold none), and any respond before the final step of apply or readback, is refused at review (see `benmore docs connector`, 'Refuse in prepare with a message').

Signing a removed member out: an apply step `- run: revoke_user_sessions` with `with: { user_id: ${{ params.<path> }} }` ends every session, API token, OAuth code and connector grant of that user in THIS app, inside the command transaction (a rollback revokes nothing; there is no window before a worker runs). `user_id` must be a `params.` path (never a literal, `user.id`, step output or loop value) naming a required, non-nullable integer in `prepared_schema`; the step is apply-only, not allowed inside `for_each`, and refused in ordinary flows. It is refused (the whole apply rolls back, class `denied`) when the target is the acting user, a framework admin (users.role or a global admin grant), or did not hold a live membership row (groups.table, soft-delete and active_field honored, email-keyed rows only for a verified account) in the actor's selected tenant when the apply began; checking at the start covers a membership the same apply removes, before or after the step. An app without `groups:` or an actor without a selected tenant is always refused. The review page lists the step so the approver sees it, and an `approval: grant` command carrying it is auto-approved like any other. It writes one `mcp_command_revoke_sessions` audit row (ids only, no address). A target who is also a member of another tenant is signed out of it too (sessions are not tenant-bound).
Removed command: a valid reload that removes a command tool leaves that tool's pending operations unusable (commit and status answer denied, business data unchanged).
